svg.title: 1970s Détente Architecture: Superpower Pressures, SALT 1 (1972) and the Three Baskets of Helsinki (1975)
svg.desc: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History strategic diagram and geopolitical map explaining why the USA and USSR pursued Détente in the early 1970s—including the $150bn+ Vietnam War, Nixon's February 1972 China opening, the Sino-Soviet split, Soviet economic stagnation, and nuclear MAD parity—alongside SALT 1 (May 1972) and the Three Baskets of the Helsinki Accords (August 1975).

g.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · OPTION P4: SUPERPOWER RELATIONS & THE COLD WAR
1970s Détente: Superpower Pressures, SALT 1 & The Helsinki Baskets
Visited Beijing to build triangular leverage
and pressure Moscow into arms talks.
Post-1962 Cuba shock + rough ICBM parity meant both
superpowers risked total annihilation without arms limits.
millions of tonnes of US grain imports.
Having caught up with US strategic launchers,
Moscow could negotiate from equal status.
Hostile split with China made Moscow fear
diplomatic isolation against a US–China bloc.
Capped each side at 2 ABM sites (capital + 1 ICBM field),
preserving MAD deterrence by blocking missile shields.
Froze strategic land ICBMs & submarine SLBMs at existing
totals + Basic Principles pledge to avoid confrontation.
SALT 1 froze launcher tubes rather than warhead totals.
packed several nuclear warheads onto one missile—allowing
both arsenals to keep multiplying throughout the 1970s.
EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · WHY DÉTENTE STABILISED BUT DID NOT END THE COLD WAR
Détente cut war risks & boosted trade, yet rival ambitions persisted: MIRVs multiplied warheads
under SALT 1, Basket 3 human-rights clashes soured trust, and Afghanistan (Dec 1979) killed SALT 2.
